methods.method:
prep: Heat oven to 350°F; line a 9×13 pan with a parchment sling
creamed = cream until light, 3 min <- Butter @crust + Granulated Sugar @crust + Dark Brown Sugar @crust
wet = beat in <- creamed + Egg Yolks + Vanilla Bean Paste @crust
crumbs = mix on low until crumbly <- wet + Flour + Salt @crust
crust = press evenly into pan; bake 350°F 25 min until edges are golden; cool <- crumbs
cooked = bring to a boil, stirring; cook over medium, stirring often, to 245°F (firm ball) for a chewy set, 45–60 min <- Granulated Sugar @caramel + Dark Brown Sugar @caramel + Corn Syrup + Heavy Cream + Butter @caramel + Salt @caramel
caramel = off heat, stir in <- cooked + Vanilla Extract + Sarsaparilla / Root Beer Extract + Ground Star Anise
layered = pour over crust; set until firm, ~2 h <- crust + caramel
melted = melt gently <- Chocolate, White + Vanilla Bean Paste @top
spread ~2 mm thin over the caramel; sprinkle salt; set; cut 24 bars with a hot knife <- layered + melted + Flaky Sea Salt
methods.notes: Cream caramel, no condensed milk: use a 6 qt or larger pot, since the cream foams up as it boils. Temperature sets the texture: 240°F soft, 245°F chewy (cuts cleanly), 250°F firm. Keep the white-chocolate layer thin so it reads as vanilla ice cream rather than candy. Root beer caramel idea after Clever Pink Pirate (https://cleverpinkpirate.com/root-beer-caramel-recipe/). Bars are large (~70 g); cut 48 for cookie-box size.
